```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
load( "../results/aggregated_simulation_results.RData" )
require(tidyverse)

ESTIMAND_LEVELS <- c("stu", "dstu", "sch", "dsch")
ESTIMATOR_LEVELS <- c("LR w/ CRSE", "LR (agg, wt)", "DB_indiv (FE)", "DB_indiv (int)",
                      "LR (agg)", "DB_clust (int)", "DB_clust (FE)",
                      "MLM")
```

## Overview

This is just a quick note illustrating results from the "initial" simulations:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
scenarios = expand.grid( 
  K = c(10), 
  J.bar = c(20,50),
  p.bar = c(0.5),
  ATE.district = 0.2, 
  sd.district = 0.1,
  ICC.district = 0.2,
  variable.J = c(T,F),
  variable.p = c(T,F),
  
  # cluster-level params
  n.bar = c(50), 
  sd.school = c(0.1), 
  ICC.school = 0.2,
  variable.n = c(T,F),
  
  # size and correlation params
  size.impact.cor.district = c(0,0.75),
  size.impact.cor.school = c(0,1),
  proptx.impact.cor.district = c(0,0.75))
```

Key for estimand names:

* "stu": student-weighted
* "sch": school-weighted
* "dstu": district-weighted student-weighted
* "dsch": district-weighted school-weighted

\newpage

## Absolute bias

There are three groups of methods:

1. Student-weighted: LR w/ CRSE, LR (agg, wt), DB_indiv (int), DB_indiv (FE).
These methods have less bias for the student-weighted estimands. 

2. School-weighted: LR (agg), DB_clust (int), DB_clust (FE).
These methods have less bias for the school-weighted estimands.

3. MLM: about 90% of the way down the spectrum from student-weighted to school-weighted (i.e., slightly different from school-weighted).

The differences between the student and school-weighted methods are proportionally smaller for the district-weighted versions of those estimands. 

For clarity I've removed the bias for superpopulation estimands here, since true finite-sample and superpopulation estimand averages are the same.

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("bias"), ~mean(abs(.)))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("bias")) %>%
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"),
                           levels = ESTIMAND_LEVELS),
         method = factor(method, levels = ESTIMATOR_LEVELS)) %>% 
  filter(finite) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid( ~ estimand) +
  coord_flip()
```

Old tables:

```{r}
bias.table
```


## RMSE

Similar to bias results, but MLM is just uniformly slightly better than everything else, for every estimand.

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("RMSE"), ~mean(abs(.)))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("RMSE")) %>%
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = as.factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(finite ~ estimand) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0.05, 0.081))
```

Old tables:

```{r}
RMSE.table
```

\newpage

## SE

The student-weighted methods generally have greater estimated and true standard errors.

In general, methods' estimated standard errors tend to be similar to their finite-sample standard errors.
As expected, methods' true finite-sample standard errors are less than their true superpopulation standard errors.

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("SE."), ~mean(.)), 
            mean.SE.hat = mean(mean.SE.hat)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("SE")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value, group=name, fill=name)) +
  geom_col(position="dodge") +
  coord_flip(ylim=c(0.05, 0.07))
```

Note: unlike the results table below, the plot above is not normalized, so different simulation scenarios will have different true SEs.

Old tables:

```{r}
SE.table
```

## Coverage

Is generally sub-nominal.

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarize(across(starts_with("cover"), mean)) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("cover")) %>% 
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = as.factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(finite ~ estimand) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0.95),
             lty="dashed", color="red") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0.5, 1))
```

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("cover")) %>% 
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = as.factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(finite ~ estimand) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0.95),
             lty="dashed", color="red") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0.5, 1))
```

## Next steps

A few initial impressions:

1. All of the true estimands tend to be super close to the overall average of 0.2.

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("ATE."), mean))
sruns %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("ATE."), sd))
```

Presumably more torturing of the simulation parameters can lead to more extreme results, which I'll do next.
This will also help clarify what the methods target.


2. Some strange bias results.
While average *absolute* bias follows as we'd expect, average bias produces:

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("bias"), ~mean(.))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("bias")) %>%
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = as.factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"))) %>% 
  filter(finite) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid( ~ estimand) +
  coord_flip()
```

Here, the district-school-weighted, school-weighted, and student-weighted results remain the same, but the district-student-weighted results strangely flip such that the school-weighted estimators appear to perform better for the true district-student-weighted estimand.
I'll need to think a bit about what's going on here.


3. Other ideas?
